newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian govt, opposition to discuss race stand.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian govt, opposition to discuss race stand.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Tuesday he would hold discussions with the opposition over its proposed motion against racial intolerance.

"I think we can probably find some common ground and if we can I don't think it would do this parliament any harm to have a resolution moved by me and seconded by the leader of the opposition (Kim Beazley) on these matters," Howard told parliament.
"I'd be quite happy to have a talk to the leader of the opposition at some convenient time after hostilities have ceased at question time and see if we can't work out an arrangement."
Beazley asked the government on Monday to support a motion calling for a unified response to racial intolerance towards Aborigines and migrants.
"It (the motion) is intended to provide an opportunity for a bi-partisan endorsement of its contents," Beazley wrote in a letter to Howard.
Earlier on Tuesday, a Liberal-National coalition spokesman told reporters that Howard was unhappy with the way in which the opposition had proposed the motion.

"The Prime Minister certainly made it clear that if the leader of the opposition was genuine about bi-partisanship then he expected that he might have come to the government about the detail of any such motion," the spokesman said.
However, Howard did not comment on the specific contents of the motion at that time, the spokesman said.

The opposition's move follows controversial remarks from independent parliamentarian Pauline Hanson during the last month, in which she has attacked the government over the number of Asians in Australia and warned of an Asian invasion threat.
Howard has been criticised for not taking a stronger stand against Hanson, although he has spoken out broadly against intolerance and discriminatory immigration.
